claims.text: Plasma nitriding of Ti-6Al-4V increases surface hardness.
Plasma nitriding of Ti-6Al-4V increases wear resistance.
The treatment forms a hard, nitrogen-rich surface nitride layer.
Conventionally annealed or solution-treated-and-aged Ti-6Al-4V has a homogeneous microstructure.
A plasma-nitriding treatment at approximately 600°C for 4–6 hours is suitable for producing the proposed effect.
The proposed improvement should persist from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures during wear or friction testing under moderate loads.
Nitrogen atoms diffuse into the titanium-alloy substrate during plasma nitriding.
Diffused nitrogen reacts with titanium to form a surface layer composed primarily of titanium nitrides such as TiN.
The surface nitride phases are hard and stable.
The nitride phases act as a barrier to wear and abrasion.
The nitride barrier causes higher surface hardness and better wear resistance than in untreated Ti-6Al-4V.
Plasma nitriding may increase measured surface hardness by approximately 20–50% relative to untreated material.
Untreated Ti-6Al-4V has lower surface hardness than plasma-nitrided Ti-6Al-4V under comparable conditions.
Untreated Ti-6Al-4V has a higher wear rate than plasma-nitrided Ti-6Al-4V under comparable conditions.
Excessive treatment temperature or exposure could cause unwanted grain growth or internal stresses that impair core properties.
The magnitude of improvement depends on plasma-nitriding parameters and the initial titanium-alloy microstructure.
Nitride-layer uniformity and adhesion may vary with processing details.
